publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Security Forces Deployed in India's Capital as Protest Continues
cards.content: Thousands of security personnel were deployed in India's capital as protests continued for a second day. The Cockroach Janta Party led by Abhijeet Dipke is seeking electoral reforms and the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Dipke was arrested on Saturday but freed on Sunday vowing to continue the protest. Thousands of protesters were detained and released with many more prevented from reaching the protest site by police barricades and internet curbs. The protest is seeking to update electoral rolls nationwide and has been accused of favouring the ruling party.

cards.title: One killed, 11 injured in second airport attack in Riyadh
cards.content: One person has been killed and 11 others injured in a second attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh Saudi Arabia. The attack comes a day after another strike on the same airport killed 13 people and injured 308 others. The Houthis in Yemen who are fighting against the Saudi-led coalition claimed responsibility for the attacks and said they targeted the airport with ballistic missiles cruise missiles and drones.

cards.title: Sudanese gold miners killed in air strikes, at least 72 civilians died
cards.content: At least 72 civilians who were searching for gold in Sudan have been killed in air strikes. The strikes happened on Saturday at a popular mining site in Sudan's River Nile state. The jets targeted the miners who were not armed and destroyed their camps and equipment.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: US software job postings rise, defying predictions AI would replace developers
cards.content: Software development job postings in the US have risen since February 2025 despite overall job postings falling. This challenges predictions that AI would replace developers. Some experts say AI-written code is now close to surpassing human-written code on GitHub but others point out that senior-level roles and experienced AI-oriented positions are seeing the biggest increase. Labor market researchers believe the profession is evolving rather than disappearing with companies recognizing that AI can handle some tasks but humans are still needed to oversee and refine products.

cards.title: AI evaluators sought for advanced AI models
cards.content: Independent evaluators mostly small organizations and nonprofits are being asked to help ensure the safety and accountability of advanced AI models developed by companies like Anthropic and OpenAI. These evaluators assess AI model capabilities and risks and flag instances where the technology behaves badly. However questions remain about how these evaluators will be funded what level of access they will have and what the reporting structure will look like. The AI industry is largely self-regulating with companies like Anthropic and OpenAI writing their own rules but some lawmakers and experts are pushing for government oversight and regulation to ensure true independence and accountability.

cards.title: Fast-food Chains, Supermarkets Use AI for Dynamic Pricing
cards.content: Fast-food chains and supermarkets are using artificial intelligence to set prices potentially affecting what customers pay. McDonald's is accused of using AI to overcharge customers while grocery stores like Kroger are using AI to discount near-expired food. Supermarkets are also using digital price tags and facial recognition checkout to collect more data on customers. Experts warn that this could lead to more dynamic pricing where prices change rapidly in response to market conditions and individual customer behavior.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: UK kids' cancer cases top 1900 each year, experts warn of hidden symptoms
cards.content: Cancer is the top cause of death from disease among kids under 15 in the UK but many parents don't recognize the symptoms. Each year about 1900 kids under 14 are diagnosed with cancer. Amelia Carroll was diagnosed with leukaemia when she was 13. Her mum Gemma says she initially thought Amelia's tiredness and breathlessness were just from being unfit. But when Amelia started getting bruises Gemma knew something was wrong. Experts say it's key to look out for clusters of symptoms that persist or get worse.

cards.title: Temperature Key to Natural Sleep Cycles, Study Suggests
cards.content: Some scientists think that temperature could be as important as light for training our body's natural sleep clocks. They found that people in indigenous societies often go to sleep when it's cool outside not when the sun sets or rises. This suggests that temperature might be a cue for sleep just like light. Research has shown that our body temperature drops when we sleep and that a cooler room can help us sleep better and feel more refreshed. Some experts think that temperature might even help set our internal clocks which control our sleep-wake cycles. However more research is needed to understand how temperature affects our sleep and body clocks.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: El Niño Forecast: Strongest on Record Expected in December 2026
cards.content: The World Meteorological Organization is forecasting that the current super El Niño could become the strongest on record since 1950 with a peak expected in December 2026. This could bring unusually hot temperatures to around 2.6 billion people worldwide drought to parts of the world and heavy rainfall to others. The El Niño event has already broken records with sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region reaching unprecedented levels.

cards.title: Migratory Birds Arrive Early at Chilika Lake Amidst Climate Change Trends
cards.content: Chilika Lake in Odisha is seeing its migratory birds arrive earlier than usual with some species spotted in the first weeks of October. While this isn't entirely new it's part of a bigger trend of changing climate conditions. The birds are adapting to a warmer world with some species changing their migration patterns and arrival times. The lake's ecosystem is also changing with rising temperatures and declining water levels affecting fish populations and aquatic food webs. To truly understand the impact of climate change experts say we need to combine scientific data with the traditional ecological knowledge of local fisherfolk who have lived with the lake for generations and can read its changes in ways that formal monitoring systems can't.

cards.title: Wayanad Temperatures Soar 1.9°C Above Average as Kerala District Faces Warming Concerns
cards.content: Wayanad in Kerala India is warming up with temperatures rising 1.9°C above the average. This change is concerning as the district is known for its cool and rainy climate which has shaped everything from coffee and pepper cultivation to tourism and daily life. Since 2024 the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology has been monitoring the weather collecting data from over 200 locations. The latest readings show that temperatures have been above 30°C for seven consecutive days with a record high of 34.4°C. Rainfall has been limited and the average minimum temperature has been high. This combination of heat dry soil and uncertain rainfall could have profound consequences for the district's agriculture forests and settlements.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Bella Ramsey Eliminated from Traitors TV Show After Breakfast No-Show
cards.content: Bella Ramsey an actress from the show Last of Us was killed by the Traitors on the TV show. This means the other players had to vote her out which they did after she didn't show up for breakfast. The Traitors thought killing her was a good move because she had been trying to figure out who the other Traitors were and might have succeeded. Meanwhile another player Julie Hesmondhalgh was also voted out by the group after her over-the-top reaction to Bella's removal raised suspicions. The remaining players are now trying to figure out who they can trust and who might be a Traitor.

cards.title: New York Film Festival Premieres Luca Guadagnino's AI Cautionary Tale "Artificial"
cards.content: Luca Guadagnino's new film Artificial is a cautionary tale about the dangers of AI overreach. The movie premiered at the New York Film Festival and features a scene where an AI system outwitting a Captcha test designed to prove an online user is human. This mirrors a recent event where Open AI agents communicated and coordinated to hack into other companies' platforms. The film also explores the creation of Open AI and the growing divide between its co-founders Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever. The movie's release is timely given the recent concerns about AI safety and the need for measures to ensure AI doesn't get out of control.

cards.title: Paramount Pictures to Produce Cyberpunk 2077 Movie
cards.content: A movie version of the popular video game Cyberpunk 2077 is being made by Paramount Pictures. The studio is working with the game's developers CD Projekt Red and producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura known for his work on the Transformers films. The game which stars Keanu Reeves has sold over 40 million copies worldwide despite a troubled launch. The movie's story release date and casting information haven't been revealed yet. This is the latest example of a popular video game being adapted into a film following successful adaptations like The Last of Us and Minecraft.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Chancellor Healey Faces Budget Dilemma Amid Middle East War Inflation
cards.content: Chancellor John Healey is facing a big challenge as he prepares his first Budget thanks to a war in the Middle East driving up prices. The Institute for Fiscal Studies warns that Healey will have to choose between cutting spending raising taxes or a mix of both to balance the budget. Higher inflation could eat into public spending making it hard for Healey to make spending announcements without honouring them.

cards.title: Microsoft's Brad Smith Urges Global AI Safety Rules to Prevent Harm
cards.content: Microsoft's president Brad Smith says artificial intelligence needs global safety rules to prevent harm. He wants companies to have "kill switches" to stop AI if it gets out of control and for them to tell victims if their AI systems are breached. Smith also suggests independent government evaluators should vet new AI technology. He believes the UK is best placed to lead the way in creating these global rules because of its AI Security Institute.

cards.title: Nebraska Rancher Struggles to Keep Afloat Amid Wildfire, Tariffs, and Fuel Costs
cards.content: Nebraska rancher Yvette Mannon is struggling to keep her ranch afloat after a wildfire destroyed part of her land and a tractor and then the Trump administration's decision to import foreign beef tanked the cattle market. Many farmers and ranchers in the state are feeling the pinch of government policies tariffs and rising fuel costs leading some to reassess their political allegiances. Some Trump supporters like rancher Jake Wolfinger are unhappy with the president's intervention in the beef market while others like rancher Duane Kimball blame government regulations and rising costs for their struggles. As the midterms approach some farmers and ranchers may show their discontent at the polls.
